geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the blunt cantilever with a split-wing massing so the building can hold a public ground seam instead of reading as a sealed stepped block.
Keep the split aligned with the long bar direction to preserve one dominant gesture.
Open a meaningful central gap to create a public void rather than a superficial notch.
Retain a continuous base condition so the split remains one hierarchy and not fragmented volumes.
Introduce a courtyard macro anchored to the dominant mass so the access edge can become publicly legible.
Size the courtyard as a real program-supporting void.
Aim the void toward the access side to satisfy the public-threshold requirement.

graph_edits.rationale: Split the primary bar into a more legible active base and upper mass so the ground relationship can respond to the access edge instead of remaining a sealed stacked block.
Keep the dominant bar orientation stable while improving hierarchy through section articulation rather than plan fragmentation.
Add a real public void to create an active ground threshold and usable open space tied to the neighborhood-living brief.
Use a moderate courtyard margin so the void remains legible and not merely decorative.
Open the new void toward the verified access side to restore frontage alignment and public entry legibility.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass with a modest top-step and some overall continuity, but it fails the program contract because the visible form does not establish a convincing active ground threshold on the verified access edge and the void/courtyard logic is too weak to support neighborhood-living semantics. Across views the object is coherent, yet the section is more like a generic stepped block than a building with a legible public ground zone or meaningful terrace/cut responding to access. The silhouette is acceptable but not especially resolved; the main issue is semantic rather than formal fragmentation. Reference 1 supports the idea of a coherent stacked mass, reference 2 suggests a controlled vertical taper as a transferable hierarchy move, and reference 3 is only weakly relevant for frontage cues.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this neighborhood-living candidate; the reference’s urban podium/tower condition should not be copied literally.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous stacked mass can still read as one dominant gesture if the section is legible and the base remains coherent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology and scale are not appropriate to directly imitate for a compact mixed neighborhood building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A slender, slightly torqued vertical profile can give hierarchy and a clear top without fragmenting the mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Primarily a very different low-rise commercial object; useful only for frontage/threshold logic, not overall massing.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low horizontal mass with an attached accent can create active ground presence and a readable entry edge.

warnings: The mass appears too sealed on the access side for the stated active-edge requirement.
No clearly legible public void, court, or entry seam is visible at the road frontage.
The form is coherent but reads more like a generic stepped block than neighborhood-living architecture.
